{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011Cg6WY33dTsZvjRLVexES6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The benchmark in `unstructured/` is now OpenMP-parallel, with results bit-identical to the original for every configuration I tested, including odd and even iteration counts, tiny grids, and the `-r` output path.\n\n**What changed in `unstructured.cpp`**\n\n- **Simulation loop.** One parallel region spans all iterations, with a static `omp for` over elements inside. Each iteration costs a single barrier instead of a fork/join, and every thread keeps the same contiguous element slice in its own caches. Buffers are swapped as thread-local pointers, with the vectors swapped once at the end so the caller sees the same final state as before. The flux arithmetic is untouched, so floating-point results are identical.\n- **NUMA first touch.** The vectors now use a default-init allocator so `resize()` no longer zero-fills on the main thread. The parallel init loop in `buildSquare2D` touches each page with the thread that will later process it. Before this fix, all memory sat on one socket and the second socket was slower than useless.\n- **Thread pinning.** Each thread pins itself to one CPU of the process affinity mask. Unbound threads at full machine occupancy were migrating constantly and the per-iteration barrier became very expensive. If you set `OMP_PROC_BIND`, `OMP_PLACES`, or `GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY` yourself, the program defers to that.\n- **Hash.** The result hash is a parallel XOR reduction, which is exact regardless of thread count.\n- The program also prints the OpenMP thread count in its header.\n\n**CMakeLists.txt** now requires OpenMP and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. The executable name is unchanged and no files were added.\n\n**Performance on this box** (2-socket EPYC 7763, 128 cores, 256 hardware threads, default environment):\n\n| Case | Serial | OpenMP |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512x512, 100 iterations | 233 ms | 4 ms |\n| 4096x4096, 50 iterations | 7903 ms | 643 ms |\n\nThe large case is memory-bandwidth bound: the static element struct is 144 bytes per element and is streamed every iteration. Running with 128 threads, one per physical core, is slightly faster still at 564 ms. I kept the data structures as-is to preserve the reported memory usage and semantics.\n\nThe validation sums in `validateResults` stay serial. They are outside the timed region and a parallel floating-point reduction could change the printed low digits."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":489,"cache_read_input_tokens":43316,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":489},"output_tokens":739,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0913f798-99ca-4882-a92d-b437d63d48ce","uuid":"fbcab855-8192-4be1-8639-cde0b195e809","timestamp":"2026-10-16T20:00:21.509Z","request_id":"req_011Cg6WY2fKRmscDLZfGaqxc"}

The executable name is unchanged and no files were added.\n\n**Performance on this box** (2-socket EPYC 7763, 128 cores, 256 hardware threads, default environment):\n\n| Case | Serial | OpenMP |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512x512, 100 iterations | 233 ms | 4 ms |\n| 4096x4096, 50 iterations | 7903 ms | 643 ms |\n\nThe large case is memory-bandwidth bound: the static element struct is 144 bytes per element and is streamed every iteration. Running with 128 threads, one per physical core, is slightly faster still at 564 ms. I kept the data structures as-is to preserve the reported memory usage and semantics.\n\nThe validation sums in `validateResults` stay serial.
